CFDocument.title: GACE® Special Education General Curriculum Assessment Test

CFItems.fullStatement: Development and Characteristics of Learners
Planning the Learning Environment and Social Interactions
Instruction
Assessment
Foundations and Professional Responsibilities
*Objective 1: Understands human development and applies knowledge to needs of and influences on learners with disabilities*
*Objective 1: Understands and applies knowledge of curriculum development and lesson planning*
*Objective 2: Understands and applies knowledge of how to organize, manage, and monitor the learning environment*
*Objective 1: Understands and applies knowledge of effective teaching strategies and techniques and uses of technology*
*Objective 1: Understands definitions and types of assessments and applies knowledge to interpretation and uses of data*
*Objective 1: Understands legal definitions and requirements and uses knowledge of the law to ensure rights of stakeholders*
*Objective 2: Understands the professional roles of teachers and others and develops ways to collaborate and communicate*
Understands human development and behavior; e.g., cognitive, language, social/emotional, psychological, academic, physical development
Identifies stages of human development and behavior
Understands and differentiates among theoretical approaches to student learning and motivation

Identifies the basic characteristics and defining factors for each of the major disability categories under which individuals age three through 21 may be eligible for services under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA)
Understands the impact of disabilities on individuals, families, and society across the life span
Understands how language, cultural, and gender differences can affect the identification process
Understands co-occurring conditions
Recognizes how family systems and the role of families contribute to the development of an individual with a disability
Demonstrates what influences may have an effect on the development and achievement of an individual with a disability
Understands the characteristics of lesson plans
Knows the elements of lesson plans
Develops learning objectives that are measurable and appropriate
Knows the means of providing access to the curriculum
Knows how to organize the learning environment
Understands theory and practice of effective classroom management
Knows how to design and maintain a safe and supportive classroom environment that promotes student achievement
Knows basic health, nutrition, and safety management procedures for students
Knows and understands instructional strategies and techniques
Recognizes grouping formats that promote individual academic success
Implements strategies to facilitate the maintenance and generalization of concepts learned across settings, considering students’ ages and abilities
Implements strategies to facilitate the generalization of concepts learned across curricula, considering students’ ages and abilities
Selects and implements research-based interventions for individual students
Uses resources to select and implement research-based interventions
Knows how to select, develop, and evaluate developmentally and functionally appropriate materials, equipment, and environments
Knows how to use technology to support instruction
Demonstrates knowledge of transitions and transition planning
Recognizes assessments that are effective and appropriate
Knows the definitions and uses of various assessments
Interprets a variety of assessment data
Understands and uses the results of assessments
Knows federal definitions
Knows federal requirements for the referral and identification process
Knows federal safeguards of the rights of stakeholders (parents, local education agency [LEA], students, teachers, related service providers)
Knows the components of a legally defensible Individualized Education Program (IEP)
Knows major legislation that affects the field of special education
Understands the roles and responsibilities of the special education teacher
Understands the roles and responsibilities of other professionals and those who deliver related services
Understands strengths and limitations of various collaborative approaches within the general classroom and the special education classroom
Communicates to stakeholders the progress of students, using language and terms the stakeholders will likely understand
Identifies potential bias that may impact teaching and interactions with students and their families
